notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.

**Before recording anything:** the Qube team connects Qube to Claude on Joshua's laptop (same setup as J022) and he has a Qube login. Don't show any install commands, API keys, emails, account names or file paths. Every chatbot recording is on Joshua's own accounts, logged in, with notifications off.

**Reuse from M05:** the tier board, the "QUANT TRADING" pill, the "I'm biased" big text, M05's big-text style (used for A5 with new words) and the caption style are M05's own. Duplicate them from the M05 CapCut project and swap only the logos, names and the A5 words. If the M05 project isn't available, build them from the specs below.

open.text: **CTA.** Line 11 is M05's ending word for word, as you asked: "…comment QUBE and I'll send you the full breakdown." The Breakdown DM isn't live in ManyChat yet (P6), so today the DM sends only the link. If you'd rather not wait: "…or comment QUBE and I'll send you the link for the free sign-up."
**Example stock in the inserts.** A4 and A6 use Apple as the search and question, only as news, never a call. Say if you'd rather use another.

Frame head and chest in the lower two thirds, leaving the top third (640px) clear above his head for the board. 3. Record the hook twice, clean. 4. Record lines 1–11 in one take. Say each tier word on its own with a short beat after it: "F tier." "D tier." 5. Move the phone in close and record, three times each: "See the problem?" · "That number looks insane. Totally made up."

rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, https://www.perplexity.ai logged in. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Type exactly: `What moved the S&P 500 this week?` 4. Press Enter. Record until the answer is done and its numbered sources are on screen. Hold 3s on the sources. 5. 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, https://claude.ai logged in, a new chat. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Hold 2s on the code. **CHECK: stop the recording before Claude runs anything or shows any result. Only the code is on screen.**

1. Terminal app, dark theme, font 22, full screen. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Type `claude`, press Enter. 4. Hold 2s on the screen that shows Qube is connected. 5. Type exactly, by hand, don't paste: `Using Qube, build a strategy that buys the S&P 500 when it drops 2% in a day. Sell once it's up 2% from where I bought, or if it falls another 3%. Test it on the last five years.` 6. Press Enter. Keep recording into A10. **CHECK: no email, key, file path or account name on screen at any point.**

lines.text: I ranked 6 tools for building a trading strategy from S to F, so you don't have to.
Quant trading just means trading with rules and data instead of your gut.
And yes, I am biased because we built one.
Asking chat GPT what to buy.
F tier.
You're just getting an opinion that nobody has actually tested.
Excel.
D tier.
You can test a strategy on past prices in a spreadsheet, but one wrong sell and your test is secretly using tomorrow's price to make today's trade.
Your results look amazing, but they're fake.
Meta trader.
C tier.
It's popular for Forex, which is trading currencies like the dollar and the euro.
But to build a bot that trades for you, it needs to learn its own coding language.
Trading view.
B tier.
Really good charts and it can test strategies on past prices.
But to do that, you need to learn its coding language.
Pinescript.
Quant connect.
A tier.
Very powerful for testing strategies, but you have to write real code in Python or C-sharp.
Notice the pattern?
Everything from C to A wants you to be a programmer.
Cube.
S tier.
You describe the idea in plain English.
It turns it into exact rules, tests them on past prices and runs it.
No code required.
The hard part of trading should be the idea, not learning how to code.
Disagree?
Drop your tier list in the comments or comment cube and I'll send you the full breakdown.
